variants.title: Pulsed NMR inversion recovery: glycerin (illustrative T1)
variants.note: A viscous liquid relaxes fast: T1 is tens of milliseconds, so the delays are short.

source.title: Bloch relaxation formulas; the T1 and T2 of this sample are chosen for the lab (unsourced / illustrative)

variants.title: Pulsed NMR inversion recovery: water with paramagnetic ions (illustrative T1)
variants.note: Paramagnetic ions shorten T1 of the water protons from seconds to a fraction of a second.

source.title: Bloch relaxation formulas; the T1 and T2 of this sample are chosen for the lab (unsourced / illustrative)

variants.title: Pulsed NMR Hahn echo: mineral oil (illustrative T2)
variants.note: A pi/2 - tau - pi sequence refocuses the static-field inhomogeneity; the echo height falls as exp(-2 tau/T2).

source.title: Bloch relaxation formulas; the T1 and T2 of this sample are chosen for the lab (unsourced / illustrative)

variants.title: Pulsed NMR Hahn echo: water with paramagnetic ions (illustrative T2)
variants.note: A shorter T2 than T1: the transverse magnetisation dephases faster than the longitudinal one recovers.

source.title: Bloch relaxation formulas; the T1 and T2 of this sample are chosen for the lab (unsourced / illustrative)

variants.title: Pulsed NMR CPMG train in a field gradient (illustrative T2)
variants.sample: Water with paramagnetic ions in a 2 mT/m gradient (unsourced / illustrative)
variants.note: In a field gradient a single Hahn echo also loses height to diffusion; the CPMG train (closely spaced pi pulses) measures T2 without it.

source.title: Bloch relaxation formulas; the T1 and T2 of this sample are chosen for the lab (unsourced / illustrative)
